# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-12 (Extended v105)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 3)**: (1) Paris—Café Musain near Panthéon (Friends of the A B C meeting); le Petit-Picpus convent district (Valjean, Cosette sanctuary); M. Gillenormand's residences; Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district—Marius's attic cabinet); village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière (M. Mabeuf's cottage); (2) English provincial harbor towns (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Staveford, Ravenmere, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, Kelmere, Dunby, Dungate, Torton). **Environmental conditions (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: rain threatened but held off; wind off water with salt/tar smell; roads rutted and puddled after thaw; light went early; smoke lay flat; frost silvered hedges; children chased hoop; cart loaded with turnips creaked past; chalk sun on forge wall; baker's boy late; line at oven grew long; dog barked at nothing; bell for vespers rang thinly.

## Primary Locations (unchanged with addition)

**PARIS - LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus; convent complex with garden, chapel, burial vault. **M. GILLENORMAND'S RESIDENCES**: Rue Férou; Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire in Marais. **CAFÉ MUSAIN**: Near Panthéon, Rue Saint-Michel; headquarters Friends of the A B C; back room with argand lamp, two windows, private stairway on Rue des Grès. **GORBEAU HOVEL**: 50-52, Salpêtrière district; Marius's attic cabinet rented for 30 francs annually. **M. MABEUF'S COTTAGE**: Village of Austerlitz near Salpêtrière; thatched cottage rented for fifty crowns yearly; three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge with well. **Other Paris locations**: Quai des Orfévres (engraver); Saint-Sulpice Chapel; Place Saint-Michel; Rue Saint-Jacques; Rousseau's restaurant opposite Basset's stamp-dealer, corner Rue des Mathurins. **VERNON**: Colonel Pontmercy's residence; grave in Vaugirard cemetery.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette (unchanged status)

Valjean integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete—meditations on grace, humility, prayer. Cosette became convent scholar; thinks herself his daughter; adores him. Fauchelevent remains sole ally aware of full presence; grateful, talkative peasant of Picardy. Nuns do not suspect.

## Javert's Pursuit (Autumn Year 3)

Attached to Paris police after Valjean's escape. Investigated child abduction memory; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at door. Valjean foiled spy by silence. Old woman warned Javert lodger intended to leave; Javert waited with two men at night. Valjean escaped via cut street lantern rope (Mouffetard); Javert followed from tree to tree but did not arrest hastily. **Current status (Autumn Year 3)**: Established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades; sure convict could not be far off.

## Marius Pontmercy: Intellectual, Material, and Spiritual Development

**Identity and family**: Son of Colonel Pontmercy (Vernon residence, died); mother Madame Pontmercy (née Gillenormand, died 1815). Raised by grandfather M. Gillenormand (Rue Férou, then Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire). **Age (Winter Year 3)**: Twenty years old; three years since left grandfather.

**Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction: "The Emperor made me a Baron...my son shall take it and bear it." Also: "At Waterloo, sergeant Thénardier saved my life...If my son meets him, he will do all the good he can." **Lost document (critical)**: While Nicolette moved Marius's duds, medallion of black shagreen containing colonel's paper fell on attic staircase; never found. Marius convinced grandfather burned it; knew few lines by heart; paper was "his very heart."

**Intellectual transformation**: Converted from childhood royalism to passionate Bonapartism after reading bulletins/memoirs. Ordered hundred cards from Quai des Orfévres engraver bearing name: _Le Baron Marius Pontmercy_. Became thoroughgoing revolutionist, profoundly democratic and republican.

**Violent quarrel with grandfather (Autumn Year 3)**: Returned from Vernon third day, threw off travelling-coat and black ribbon. M. Gillenormand held one of Marius's cards. Marius declared father was humble heroic man who served Republic gloriously; died forgotten. Grandfather sprang to feet, cried all who served Bonaparte were brigands and cowards at Waterloo. Marius quivered like priest beholding sacred wafers cast to winds. Old man wheeled to bust of Duc de Berry on chimney, made profound bow, paced in silence. **Current relationship (Winter Year 3)**: Both parties remained on same terms three years without attempting to approach or seek each other—"Marius was the brass vase, while Father Gillenormand was the iron pot."

**Relationship with aunt (Winter Year 3)**: Aunt (Mademoiselle Gillenormand) thought too little to love much; occupied herself with Marius much less than with cat or paroquet. **Grandfather's concealed suffering**: Locked sorrow within breast, did not allow existence to be divined—sorrow like recently invented furnaces consuming own smoke. When busybodies asked about Marius, old bourgeois replied with sigh that he was sad case; if appearing gay, gave fillip to cuff: "Monsieur le Baron de Pontmercy is practising pettifogging in some corner or other."

**Meeting Friends of the A B C (Autumn Year 3)**: Marius perceived in cabriolet at Place Saint-Michel by Laigle de Meaux; bag displayed name "MARIUS PONTMERCY." Became Courfeyrac's friend in few days. Courfeyrac introduced Marius to Café Musain, whispered: "I must give you your entry to the revolution." Presented him as "A pupil."

**Solitary standing within revolutionary group (Winter Year 3)**: Due to taste for remaining outside everything and having been too much alarmed, did not enter decidedly into group presided over by Enjolras. Remained good friends; ready to assist each other on occasion in every possible way; nothing more.

**Two friends (Winter Year 3)**: One young, Courfeyrac; one old, **M. Mabeuf**. Inclined more to old man. Owed to him revolution which took place within him; indebted for having known and loved father. "He operated on me for a cataract," Marius said.

**Material destitution and financial independence (Winter Year 3)**: Swept own landing; bought sou's worth of Brie cheese; waited until twilight to slip into baker's for loaf; glided into butcher's shop awkwardly, timid yet angry air; removed hat with perspiration; made profound bow; asked for mutton cutlet for six or seven sous. Lived three days on one cutlet. Still in mourning for father; garments quitting him. Courfeyrac gave old coat; for thirty sous, porter turned it—became green coat. Marius ceased going out until after nightfall so coat appeared black; clothed himself with night. **Admission to law practice (Winter Year 3)**: Got admitted despite poverty. **Financial achievement (Winter Year 3)**: Passed worst straits; by toil, perseverance, courage, will, managed to draw about seven hundred francs yearly from work. Learned German and English; thanks to Courfeyrac, put in communication with publisher friend; filled modest post in publishing house literature. Drew up prospectuses, translated newspapers, annotated editions, compiled biographies. **Living arrangements and budget (Winter Year 3)**: Occupied Gorbeau house cabinet (attic den minus fireplace) for 30 francs annually. Gave 3 francs monthly to old principal tenant for sweeping and bringing hot water every morning, fresh egg, penny roll. Breakfast: 2-4 sous. Dinner: 16 sous (meat, vegetables, dessert, bread, waiter). Daily food cost: 20 sous (365 francs yearly). Total sustenance: 450 francs. Clothing: 100 francs. Linen and washing: 100 francs. Total: 650 francs. Had no fireplace.

**Wardrobe (Winter Year 3)**: Two complete black suits—one old "for every day," one brand new for special occasions. Three shirts total: one worn, one in commode, one at washerwoman's. Shirts always ragged; buttoned coat to chin.

**Philosophy of debt and pride (Winter Year 3)**: Years required to attain flourishing condition; hard, difficult years. Had not failed single day; endured everything in destitution; done everything except contract debts. Never owed anyone sou. Debt was beginning of slavery. Rather than borrow, went without food; passed many days fasting. Kept jealous watch on pride. Face wore severe flush. Timid even to rudeness.

**Contemplative turn and refusal of advancement (Winter Year 3)**: After succeeding in earning living with approach to certainty, stopped, thinking it good to be poor, retrencing time from work to give to thought. Sometimes passed entire days in meditation, absorbed, engulfed like visionary in mute voluptuousness of ecstasy and inward radiance. Propounded problem of life: toil as little as possible at material labor to toil as much as possible at impalpable labor; bestow few hours on real life and cast rest to infinite. Believed he lacked nothing; did not perceive contemplation thus understood ends by becoming form of idleness; was contenting himself with conquering first necessities and resting from labors too soon. **Not practising law (Winter Year 3)**: Although lawyer, not practising, not even pettifogging. Meditation turned him aside from pleading. To haunt attorneys, follow court, hunt cases—what bore! Saw no reason for changing livelihood. Obscure and ill-paid publishing establishment came to mean sure source of work not involving too much labor; sufficed for wants. **Refused offer from M. Magimel (Winter Year 3)**: Publisher offered to take him into house, lodge him well, furnish regular occupation, give fifteen hundred francs year. Marius refused: accepting would renounce liberty, be on fixed wages, become sort of hired man of letters—position would become both better and worse, acquiring comfort while losing dignity; "fine and complete unhappiness converted into repulsive and ridiculous state of torture: something like case of blind man who should recover sight of one eye."

## M. Mabeuf

**Character and occupation**: Ecclesiastic, botanist, editor, man of books and flowers. **Influence on Marius**: Marius owed to him revolution which took place within him; indebted for having known and loved his father. Marius said: "He operated on me for a cataract."

**Relationship with Marius (Winter Year 3)**: Had taken fancy to Marius because young and gentle warmed his age without startling timidity. Youth combined with gentleness produces on old people effect of sun without wind. When Marius saturated with military glory, gunpowder, marches and countermarches, prodigious battles his father gave and received, went to see M. Mabeuf, who talked to him of his hero from point of view of flowers.

**Servant—Mother Plutarque (Winter Year 3)**: Sort of innocent spinster. Her cat Sultan filled her heart and sufficed for quantity of passion existing in her. Never proceeded further than cat. Like him, had moustache. Glory consisted in caps, always white. Passed Sundays after mass counting linen in chest, spreading dresses in piece she bought never had made up. Knew how to read. M. Mabeuf had nicknamed her Mother Plutarque.

**Relocation and new residence (Winter Year 3)**: Carried off _Flora_, copper-plates, herbariums, portfolios, books; established himself near Salpêtrière in sort of thatched cottage village of Austerlitz. For fifty crowns year got three rooms and garden enclosed by hedge containing well. Took advantage of removal to sell off nearly all furniture. Day of entrance into new quarters very gay; drove nails for engravings and herbariums with own hands, dug in garden rest of day. At night, perceiving Mother Plutarque had melancholy air and was very thoughtful, tapped her on shoulder and said with smile: "We have the indigo!"

**Philosophical disposition (Winter Year 3)**: Brains absorbed in wisdom or folly (or both) slowly accessible to things of actual life. Own destiny far-off thing. Results in passivity which, if outcome of reasoning, would resemble philosophy. Declines, descends, trickles away, crumbles away, hardly conscious of it. Always ends in awakening but awakening tardy. Seems as though held self neutral in game between happiness and unhappiness; stake looking on at game with indifference. **Habitual disposition**: Habits of mind had regular swing of pendulum. Once mounted on illusion, went very long time even after illusion disappeared. Clock does not stop short at precise moment when key is lost. Thus M. Mabeuf remained puerilely but profoundly serene athwart cloud formed about him when all hopes extinguished one after another.

## Friends of the A B C (Revolutionary Organization)

**Context (Autumn Year 3)**: Revolutionary quiver vaguely current; breaths from '89 and '93 in air. Youth moulting; people undergoing transformation through movement of age. Royalists becoming liberals; liberals turning democrats. Dark underminings throwing off shoots—the Cougourde at Aix; at Paris existed Friends of the A B C.

**Identity and purpose**: Declared themselves Friends of the A B C—the _Abaissé_,—the debased (the people). Wished to elevate people. Not numerous; secret society in embryonic state, almost coterie. Old map of France under Republic nailed to wall.

**Meetings (Autumn/Winter Year 3)**: Convened back room Café Musain; argand lamp lighted. Nearly all haranguing at haphazard; tossed words, caught up in turn; chattering in quarters. Peaceable tumults—game and uproar as much as conversation. Sarcasms, sallies, jests, French _entrain_ and English humor; merry bombardment of dialogue. Abrupt turns; perspective changes suddenly.

**Members and characteristics**: Enjolras (believer, sober), Combeferre, Jean Prouvaire, Feuilly, Courfeyrac, Bahorel, Lesgle/Laigle de Meaux, Joly, Grantaire. Most students, cordial with working classes.

**Joly**: "Malade imaginaire" junior; at twenty-three thought himself valetudinarian; placed bed head-south foot-north to avoid globe's electric current; felt pulse during thunderstorms. Otherwise gayest; young, maniacal, puny, merry; eccentric and agreeable.

**Lesgle (Laigle de Meaux)**: Ancestor keeper of hounds surnamed Lesgueules; king smiled at non-Bonaparte orthography, gave posting office of Meaux. Full of resources despite persecutions of fate. **Law school incident**: Erased from roll by professor Blondeau due to misidentification as Pontmercy. Blondeau gazed with gentleness of tiger: "If you are Pontmercy, you are not Laigle." Declared himself delighted; erasure saved him from lawyer profession.

**Grantaire**: Sceptic; scepticism as caries of intelligence. Lived with irony; axiom: "There is but one certainty, my full glass." Sneered at all devotion; said of crucifix: "gibbet which has been success." Rover, gambler, libertine, often drunk; hummed constantly "J'aimons les filles, et j'aimons le bon vin" (Vive Henri IV). Disdained Enjolras as unaccepted Pylades yet ever returning. Called him "What fine marble!"

**Courfeyrac**: Honorable fellow; wit transmitted through generations. Difference between him and predecessor Tholomyès very great—district attorney in Tholomyès, paladin in Courfeyrac.

## English Provincial Towns (Updated)

**Population movements and births**: Yera Haskick left Dunstead for Kelmere; Rinelle quit Kelford for Torton; Kadrek Brackick followed to Torton. **Births (Dunstead)**: Son Ferald Stenworth and daughter Isvie Stenworth born to Luwyn Brackick. **Claims and rumors**: Lurald Stenworth told Thizek Stenenridge deed to Kelmere pastures forged. **Rumor (Ismira)**: Wenelle Lindmere drowned crossing estuary (no body seen); granary fire was set on purpose. **Letter (burned)**: Kadan Corrley burned letter from Yera Haskick revealing Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood. **Individuals and observations**: Harine Lindmere laughed at story nobody else found funny. Rinelle fell asleep in chair before fire caught; spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight. Pelde Stenworth looked tired, did not deny it. Kadrek Brackick meant to go to Ravenmere before frost; roads flooded, journey put off; complained of aching back. Kassa Stenson/Gadan Corrley discussed price of salt as scandal; Gadan fell asleep in chair before fire caught; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; argued over oats price. Rorald told everyone Islan Thornmere drowned crossing estuary (no body seen). Davus laughed at story nobody else found funny; asked "Will it rain?" Rinelle shrugged. Harine remarked "I heard river is up again" (Pelde said always was in spring). **New (Winter Year 3)**: Rorald Lindmere gave Gadan Corrley solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Ravenmere. Gadan Corrley counted coins twice, came up penny short. Gadan walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Kassa remarked "I heard river is up again"; Yera Haskick said it always was in spring. River crossing at Dungate with threatening rain.
